slides.headline: He spent his career as a government bureaucrat. He also became one of India's greatest living poets.
Sitakant Mahapatra
slides.body: Born September 17, 1937 in Odisha, Mahapatra joined the Indian Administrative Service in 1961 and served until his retirement in 1995 - a full career inside the government, running alongside a second career most colleagues never attempted.

slides.eyebrow: What he built in the other career
slides.headline: 15+ poetry collections, and India's highest literary honor.
slides.body: Mahapatra won the 1974 Sahitya Akademi Award, then the Jnanpith Award in 1993 - India's highest literary honor. He also spent years researching the tribal oral traditions of Eastern Odisha, work most of his readers never saw.

slides.eyebrow: Why it matters for Viksit Bharat 2047
slides.headline: Two Padma honors followed, decades apart.
slides.body: He received the Padma Bhushan in 2002 and the Padma Vibhushan in 2011 - both for literature, both arriving well after his government career had already ended. A bureaucrat's file doesn't usually outlive his poetry. His did the opposite.
